newsitem.title: HONG KONG: PLA reinforcements likely in HK before handover.
newsitem.headline: PLA reinforcements likely in HK before handover.

text.p: Chinese People's Liberation Army (PLA) forces in Hong Kong are likely to be reinforced by several hundred more troops ahead of the colony's handover to Beijing on June 30, Britain's chief negotiator said on Monday.

"We are making progress in our talks and certainly it is quite likely that an agreement will be reached soon. It would arrange for a number of PLA troops to arrive ahead of the transfer," British envoy Hugh Davies told Reuters.
Asked how many PLA troops might cross the border, he said: "We are not talking about a few thousand, we are talking about a few hundred".
Almost 200 PLA troops have already arrived in Hong Kong as an advance party. China has said that it wanted to send more troops ahead of the handover at midnight on June 30.
Prince Charles, heir to the British throne, will formally return Hong Kong to Chinese President Jiang Zemin, ending 156 years of colonial rule.
